text: Modeling Notes, Data-Quality Caveats & Links to Existing Pipeline Work |

Overall data character | This is a discovery-stage preclinical pharmacology paper (in vitro cell lines + xenograft), not a clinical biomarker study. There is no human PK/PD, no biopsy-based biomarker data, and no formal model fitting in the original paper — all effect summaries are pairwise statistics (t-test, log-rank) on raw assay readouts. Anything built from it is a preclinical mechanistic scaffold to later bridge to clinical data.

Single-dose kinetics limitation | Every western blot time course (Figs 2C, 2D, 3B, 3C) and the Fig 4 transcriptional panel use ONE fixed concentration (100 nM). This is enough to fit turnover/delay kinetics at that dose but NOT a dose-response surface at the target-modulation or transcriptional tiers. Dose-response is only available at the phenotypic level (Figs 1, 2A/B) and combination level (Fig 6).

Western blots are qualitative unless redensitometered | None of the immunoblots report numeric band intensities — only representative images. If your modeller needs continuous values for Tier 1/2/4 western data, the practical options are: (a) treat as categorical/onset-timing evidence only, (b) do image densitometry from the embedded blot images (moderate resolution, informal precision), or (c) contact the authors for source densitometry.

Fig 4 is the strongest cascade dataset | The pathway-signature panel (13 signatures x 5 time points x 95% CI) is the only genuinely rich, quantitative, time-resolved cascade dataset in the paper. Check whether the associated microarray data were deposited in GEO (accession not stated in the visible text/references) — pulling exact values from GEO would be far more reliable than digitizing the bar chart.

Fig 1A / Fig 5 are the best endpoint datasets | Fig 1A gives printed numeric IC50s for 20 cell lines — ideal for seeding a virtual population / sensitivity-stratification layer. Fig 5A/B (tumor volume + Kaplan-Meier) are clean two-arm in vivo datasets but have no in vivo dose-ranging and no PK sampling — an exposure-response bridge will need BEZ235 PK from another source.

Connection to your existing dual-target threshold equation | You already have eq:pd_dual_target_threshold_effect validated for dactolisib/BEZ235 (dual PI3K/mTOR), using a product-of-thresholds structure: max(E_PI3K - threshold_PI3K, 0)^power_a x max(E_mTOR - threshold_mTOR, 0)^power_b. This paper is a strong data source for that equation: Fig 2A (Akt-node perturbation, no rescue) and Fig 2B (Bcl-2-node perturbation, partial plateau) are direct evidence for where each threshold sits, and Fig 6A-C combination surfaces are a validation set for the model's predicted additivity between BEZ235 and standard-of-care agents.

Recommended annotation additions before handoff | (1) Pull the GEO accession for the Fig 4 microarray data if it exists. (2) Request Supplementary Figs S1-S7 from Cancer Research online — S2 (commitment-to-death kinetics) and S4 (cell-cycle/sub-G1) would directly strengthen the Tier 4 apoptosis-execution model. (3) If precise Tier 1/2/4 kinetics are needed, plan for blot densitometry as a discrete task rather than assuming the modeller can read exact values off the images.
